questions.question: To pull away safely from a standstill on a steep uphill slope without rolling backwards, in which sequence should you operate or release these controls?

options.text: Depress F, select a gear with C, press G, and pull D.
Depress E, select a gear with C, balance the clutch until it bites while applying light pressure to G, and then release D.
Release D, press G down fully, and quickly release E to find the biting point.
Move A sharply to the left while keeping both E and F fully depressed.

questions.explanation: Diagram: A steering wheel, B indicator lever, C gear lever, D parking (hand) brake, E clutch, F brake, G accelerator. Uphill pull-away: clutch in, select gear, find the biting point with light accelerator, then release the parking brake.

questions.question: If your foot brake (F) fails completely while driving down a steep pass, which control can be used carefully as an emergency backup to slow the vehicle down, and what is the restriction?

options.text: Control C, by immediately jamming it into Reverse gear while traveling at high speed.
Control G, by pumping it rapidly to flood the engine intake.
Control D, by applying it gradually while holding the release button down to prevent the wheels from locking completely.
Control B, by switching it up and down continuously to alert other road users.

questions.explanation: If the foot brake (F) fails, apply the parking brake (D) gradually while holding the release button so the wheels do not lock.

questions.question: Which control disconnects the engine's power delivery from the drive wheels and gearbox so that you can change gears using control C?

options.text: Control F
Control G
Control E
Control A

questions.explanation: The clutch (E) disconnects engine power from the gearbox and drive wheels so you can change gear with the gear lever (C).

questions.question: When driving along a straight road and upgrading from second gear to third gear, which specific combination of controls must be used, and in what exact sequence?

options.text: Press G down firmly, move C into position, and then tap F sharply.
Release G, depress E fully, move C to the new gear position, smoothly release E, and progressively reapply G.
Keep G held down completely, depress F with your left foot, and force C into position.
Activate B to indicate the shift, move A slightly to the left, and pull up on D.

questions.explanation: Changing up: release the accelerator (G), depress the clutch (E), move the gear lever (C), release the clutch smoothly and reapply the accelerator.

questions.question: If a child suddenly runs into the road in front of your vehicle and you need to perform an immediate emergency stop to avoid a collision, which controls must you stamp down on simultaneously?

options.text: Controls D and G
Controls A and B
Controls F and E
Controls C and G

questions.explanation: In an emergency stop in a manual car, press the brake (F) and the clutch (E) at the same time.

questions.question: When parking your manual vehicle facing downhill on a steep slope, which combination of controls must be engaged to legally secure the vehicle and guarantee it cannot roll forward?

options.text: Pull up control D firmly, and use control C to select Reverse gear.
Leave control D completely down, and use control C to select Neutral.
Turn control A straight, and use control C to select First gear.
Keep control E fully depressed to the floor, and leave control C in Neutral.

questions.explanation: Parking facing downhill in a manual car: apply the parking brake (D) firmly and select reverse gear with the gear lever (C).

questions.question: You are driving on a multi-lane road and intend to move into the lane to your right. Which control do you use to signal your intention, and in which direction must it be moved?

options.text: Move control B downwards.
Move control B upwards.
Pull control D all the way up.
Turn control A sharply clockwise.

questions.explanation: To signal a move to the right, move the indicator lever (B) upwards.

questions.question: If the rear of your vehicle begins to skid or slide violently to the left on a wet road surface, which primary control must you use to correct the skid, and how should you operate it?

options.text: Stomp completely down on control G to spin the wheels out of the slide.
Pull up sharply on control D to lock the wheels completely.
Turn control A smoothly towards the left (the same direction the rear is skidding) while avoiding harsh braking on F.
Turn control A sharply to the right to force the front of the car around.

questions.explanation: Steer into the skid: if the rear slides to the left, turn the steering wheel (A) smoothly to the left and avoid harsh braking.
